name: Spin yarn with a drop spindle
blurb: Turning raw fleece into yarn with a stick and a weight. It is the oldest textile technology there is, and once it clicks it is deeply absorbing.
gear: Prepared wool roving — start with a long-staple breed
steps: Learn to draft: pull the fibres apart gently so they slide past each other into a thinner strand, without breaking it.
Attach a leader to the spindle and join your fibre to it.
Spin the spindle clockwise and let the twist travel up into the drafted fibre.
Park and draft at first — stop the spindle between your knees, draft a length, then let the twist in. Speed comes later.
Wind on to the spindle in a neat cone and continue.
Ply two singles together in the opposite direction, then set the twist by washing and hanging the skein.
tips: Too much twist makes wiry yarn that kinks; too little makes it fall apart. You are looking for the middle.
Everyone drops the spindle constantly for the first week. That is why it is called a drop spindle.
proof: A plied, twist-set skein of usable yarn that you spun from raw fibre.
